chapter: New York, the Kentucky Club and the high-hat
title: Gangsters and the Revenue men at the Kentucky Club
summary: Gangsters like Legs Diamond and Luciano frequent the club; boss Leo Bernstein relies on Greer to vet who can drink.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: We had all the gangsters, all the big gangsters you read about. Some -- he got killed.
Yeah, and all the Brooklyn gang, they'd rendevous.

You'd hear a colored boy named Slim upstairs and that's when the Revenue men were breaking down the doors, you know, because we was selling whiskey. We sold everybody, but couldn't nobody get to drink in my club unless

I give the okay, because we had a boss named Leo Bernstein, he'd come over and say, anybody want a drink. He'd say to me, you know that guy, and I'd say yeah, he's all right. Never got busted. I had a good memory. I could remember all that time, we had six hostesses, you know, just sit around with the stags.. Of course, they gig afterwards. (Laughter)
